items.note: The page proves that Phi is an isomorphism preserving cyclic convolution. It then builds the O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)) cost from the padding scans (O(Tp)), the d prefix-controlled shifts (O(dTp)) and the O(d^2) adjacent axis moves (O(V ell^tau) plus linear passes each), as the paper does at lines 4204-4292.

This is a definition and the page gives it in full: "$P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ ... and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$", after assuming pairwise coprime $s_i$. That hypothesis makes the inverse exist. Neither the page nor the paper spells out that P_i is coprime to s_i.
The page shows why the relation is respected: "Since $s_i\mid S$, each $x_i^{\mu_iS}=1$, so $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$". This is the reason the paper's bare assertion rests on.

The page argues that Phi(x^k)=1 iff s_i | mu_i k for all i. Since mu_i is a unit this means s_i | k, and pairwise coprimality then gives S | k. So x has order S and its S distinct powers exhaust the S target monomials, which is the paper's argument made explicit.
The page writes k in mixed radix with 0<=a_j<s_j. It notes "The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$" and reduces this to the paper's formula (eq:triangular-crt).
The page gives both of the paper's reasons: "Terms with $j>i$ vanish modulo $s_i$, since $s_i$ divides $P_j$, and $\mu_iP_i\equiv1$ modulo $s_i$".

The page notes that controls follow the target in storage order, so reversing the axis order puts them first. Updating i=d,...,1 then means "no lower-index control has yet changed". It also notes that each shift rotates [0,s_i) and fixes [s_i,t_i), so zero padding stays zero. The page does not give the paper's convention of using the identity when a lower-index control is invalid (line 4263-4264, outside the assigned passage); its zero-padding conclusion still holds.

The page cites the O(V ell^tau) equal-width chunk interchange and gives the leading-bit trick for widths ell and ell-1 (a fixed number of linear passes). It then sums O(d^2) moves, shows that the shifts and scans are dominated, and treats the inverse (offsets subtracted for i=1,...,d, reorder back, delete padding). The O(d^2) count of adjacent moves is asserted, as in the paper.

errors.problem: In the paper r is the polynomial length, i.e. the largest axis length t_d=r with t_i in {r/2,r} (lines 4058-4066, 1788). It is not the length of the records being moved: the page itself says those records are "each of $O(p)$ bits". The rest of the page uses r correctly as a bound on t_i and as 2^ell.
